purpose: Enumerate exact source-visible symbolic tokens in the frozen W bodies after the source-local 0.14 occurrence pass. No conventional mathematical meaning is assigned by this frontier; every token requires source-local adjudication before semantic promotion.
guards: Token kinds are lexical/source-visible only; PLUS does not assert addition, STAR does not assert Hodge duality, WORD_TENSOR does not assert tensor-product semantics, and so on.
Hyphen/minus and slash are not scanned generically because prose/names use them ambiguously; numeric fractions are recorded explicitly.

Compact named operators such as Hom(...), det(...), exp(...), conjugate(...), KAPPA(...), and source juxtaposition require a separate source-local review because their operator boundaries are not safely determined by symbol lexing alone.
A token inside an identifier, exponent, sign label, helicity label, or role name may be adjudicated NON_OPERATOR_SOURCE_TOKEN; no token is promoted automatically.
This frontier neither closes G1 nor authorizes G2.

items.body: Twistor space is C^4 / projective CP^3 with an SU(2,2) real form giving positive, negative, and null/boundary orbits for the Minkowski picture.
W01 represents Spin(4) by independent left/right SU(2)=Sp(1) actions, with the Euclidean vector action x -> g_L x g_R^{-1}; the two factors are structurally independent in Euclidean signature.

W01 identifies the common complexification of Euclidean, Minkowski, and split-signature four-vector spaces with M(2,C)=Hom(S_R,S_L), while retaining different real-form/action constraints for each signature.

W01's frame-bundle description distinguishes spin-connection one-forms from canonical/frame one-forms and uses the Palatini action integral epsilon e wedge e wedge Omega; connection variation gives torsion-free Levi-Civita structure and frame variation gives Einstein equations.
W01 identifies Euclidean projective twistor space CP3 -> S4 as the bundle whose CP1/S2 fiber parametrizes orthogonal complex structures J on each R4 tangent space, with J^2=-1.

For a chosen orthogonal complex structure J, W01 decomposes R4 tensor C into +i/-i eigenspaces and constructs S_R and S_L through exterior powers; the stabilizer U(2) lifts to SU(2)_L x U(1) with U(1) inside SU(2)_R.
On PT the lifted spinor roles have U(1) weights S_L=C^2_0 and S_R=C_-1 + C_+1 under SU(2)_L x U(1).

W01 defines the tautological line L over PT and the rank-3 quotient L^perp=C4/L; PT is SU(4)/S(U(1)xU(3)), SU(3) acts on L^perp as the color group, and the determinant-one condition fixes the relative U(1) weights.

W01 represents one Standard Model generation by Hom(l + l^perp, S_R + S_L), whose SU(3)xSU(2)_LxU(1) decomposition reproduces the listed quark/lepton transformation roles including a right-handed neutrino.

W01 identifies the t=0 compactified Minkowski S3 with the equator of Euclidean S4 and the null PT_0 locus Phi(s,s)=0; upper/lower Euclidean hemispheres correspond to positive/negative imaginary-time regions.
For free massless spinors W01 uses the Penrose transform H^1(PT_+,O(-3)) <-> Weyl solutions on S4_+ and fiber restriction H^1(CP1,O(-3))=C2 to reconstruct pointwise spinor values.

Appendix A identifies compactified complex spacetime with G_2,4(C), its tautological rank-2 bundle S and quotient S^perp, and tangent bundle TM=Hom(S,S^perp); the Klein relation omega wedge omega=0 embeds the Grassmannian into projective Lambda^2(C4).
Appendix A defines the line-plane incidence relation s^perp=Zs and the fractional-linear SL(4,C) action Z -> (C+DZ)(A+BZ)^-1; the correspondence space P(S) links PT and M.

For Euclidean twistor geometry W01 uses T=H^2, the pseudoreal map sigma with sigma^2=-1 on T and +1 projectively, HP1 homogeneous coordinates, SL(2,H) fractional-linear action, and the CP1 fibration whose sigma action is antipodal on each fiber.

W04a writes a right-handed Minkowski Weyl equation of the form (E-sigma dot p) psi_R=0, derives the Klein-Gordon mass-shell consequence, and associates its positive- and negative-energy branches with opposite helicities.
In the CP1 analogue W04b uses the three SU(1,1)=SL(2,R) orbits and hyperfunction boundary values to model the relation between holomorphic domains and Lorentzian boundary data.
In four dimensions W04b uses the SU(2,2)=Spin(4,2) action on PT with positive, negative, and null orbits; compactified Minkowski points are represented by CP1s contained in the null orbit.

For the Euclidean real form W04b uses SL(2,H)=Spin(5,1), C4=H2, and the CP3 -> HP1=S4 fibration with CP1 fibers; Wick rotation requires choosing such a Euclidean fibration and its intersection with the Minkowski null geometry.

W04d identifies the spectral positivity of time evolution with holomorphy of U(z)=exp(-izH) in a complex-time half-plane and treats this holomorphic-domain structure as the operational core of Wick rotation.

In the twistor version W04e uses a Hermitian form Phi to split projective twistor space into positive, negative, and null regions; holomorphic theory on PT+ is proposed to have boundary values on the null region representing chiral Minkowski data, with Penrose/Penrose-Ward constructions supplying part of the reconstruction machinery.

W04d explicitly contrasts the conventional complex vector carrier S_L tensor S_R with the proposed right-handed carrier S_R tensor conjugate(S_R); on the Euclidean slice the latter decomposes as a scalar plus a three-vector and SU(2)_L acts trivially.

W04d identifies conformally compactified complex spacetime with Gr(2,4,C), a spacetime point with a right-handed C2 plane in T=C4, and projective twistor space with CP3 containing the corresponding CP1.
W04d lists SU(4), SL(4,R), SL(2,H), and SU(2,2) as real forms of SL(4,C)=Spin(6,C), with the SL(2,H) and SU(2,2) forms assigned Euclidean and Minkowski geometric roles respectively.

Under the SU(2,2) real form W04d defines PT+, PT-, and PT0 by the sign of a signature-(2,2) Hermitian form; compactified Minkowski points are CP1s lying in PT0, and PT0 is the space of Minkowski light rays/celestial spheres.
Under the Euclidean SL(2,H) real form W04d uses T=C4=H2 and the CP3->HP1=S4 fibration sending each complex line to the quaternionic line it generates.

W05 distinguishes ordinary conjugation on CP1 from the twistor antipodal real structure rho_tw, with rho_tw squared equal to -1 on the C2 coordinate carrier but +1 projectively and with no projective fixed points; it also presents the same real form as a real projective conic with complex but no real points.

W05 derives rho_tw from the chosen H=C2 presentation by left multiplication by quaternion j and uses the same quaternionic mechanism on C4=H2 to define the Euclidean projective-twistor real structure.
W05 states that rho_tw on CP3 has no fixed projective points but has a four-real-dimensional family of invariant CP1 real lines parametrized by HP1=S4; each such line is a twistor P1.

W05 records the hyperkahler generalization as a sphere aI+bJ+cK of compatible complex/Kahler structures and relates the corresponding twistor spaces to hyperkahler quotients and moduli spaces generated from self-dual Yang-Mills and its dimensional reductions.

W05 presents the non-abelian Hodge example in which the hyperkahler moduli space is viewed over CP1 through lambda-connections, with lambda=1 giving ordinary flat connections and lambda=0 giving Higgs bundles.

W01 notes that anti-self-duality can be written as a moment-map zero condition and speculates about relations to twisted N=2/N=4 Yang-Mills and geometric Langlands; these are clues, not adopted dynamics of the proposal.
W02 fixes the exact Euclidean Yang-Mills normalization used in the self-dual rewrite: (1/4g^2)∫Tr(F∧*F) differs from (1/2g^2)∫Tr(F^+∧*F^+) by the topological ∫Tr(F∧F) term.

W04e defines Osterwalder-Schrader conjugation on imaginary-time test functions by Theta f(tau)=conjugate(f(-tau)), with Theta an antilinear involution, and defines the OS Hermitian form by <f,g>_OS=S2(Theta f,g).

In four dimensions W04e places chiral SU(2,2) representations in H^1(PT+,O(n-2)) and says an appropriate twistor-transform version of Theta supplies the required conjugation/reality structure for the holomorphic PT+ theory.

W04e states that the Ward-Penrose transform gives, for suitable holomorphic bundles on PT+, right-handed Weyl solutions coupled to a self-dual connection both on a Euclidean S4 hemisphere and as boundary values on Minkowski spacetime.

W02 begins from the conventional Hermitian 2x2 complex-matrix realization of Minkowski vectors, with determinant equal to minus Minkowski length-squared and Lorentz action x -> Omega_L x Omega_R^{-1}.

The conventional complex-spacetime vector representation is chirally symmetric: matrices are linear maps from the dual of the right spinor to the left spinor, equivalently the (1/2)_L tensor (1/2)_R representation.

Euclidean spacetime in the right-handed construction is a real subspace of the right-spinor tensor its conjugate, decomposing into an SU(2)_R scalar plus vector; this produces one SU(2)_R-invariant distinguished direction and a complementary three-dimensional vector subspace.

For a right-handed Minkowski Weyl degree of freedom, W02 gives the momentum-space invariant Lagrangian and associates positive-energy solutions with helicity +1/2 and negative-energy solutions with helicity -1/2.

In Euclidean signature W02 uses Hodge star squared equal to +1 to split two-forms into self-dual and anti-self-dual sectors; self-dual two-forms correspond to su(2)_R and anti-self-dual two-forms to su(2)_L. In Minkowski signature star squared is -1 and the corresponding chiral decomposition requires complexification.
W02 rewrites the Euclidean Yang-Mills action, up to the topological integral of Tr(F wedge F), using only the self-dual curvature component, and therefore only right-handed spacetime spinor geometry.
